biggestWin: Lift the context marks off the floor. --mark-ctx paints the eleven history columns and the six inside-a-fortnight dots at 1.48:1 against the card in light and 1.70:1 in dark; those marks ARE the reading, and at that ratio the twelve-week shape and the age distribution are close to invisible to anyone not looking at a good screen in good light. Ink 3 (#71717a) is already in the eighteen and clears 4.83:1 light and 3.68:1 dark against the same card, and the live column keeps its emphasis because it is darker AND indigo AND hatched. It is one token, it changes nothing else, and it is the only change on this list that alters how the whole surface reads rather than how one corner of it behaves.

findings.element: a.kpi - the four status cards in "What's quietly slipping"; rules at lately.html:323 and :325, entrance at :485, keyframes at :480
findings.problem: a.kpi carries .rise, and .rise is `animation: rise 0.5s var(--ease) both`, whose `to` step is `transform: none`. A filled animation's effect value sits above every plain author declaration in the cascade, so `a.kpi:hover { transform: translateY(-2px) }` and `a.kpi:active { transform: translateY(0) }` can never apply. Driven in chromium at 1440 in all four motion modes - settled, play, and each of those under prefers-reduced-motion - the card's computed transform is matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0) and its rendered top is 629.55px at rest, under the pointer, and while the pointer is held down: identical to two decimal places in all twelve readings. The only thing that moves is the border, rgba(17,17,17,0.055) to rgba(17,17,17,0.10), which is 1.06:1 to 1.12:1 against the card it sits on. This file documents the same cascade trap twice and routes around it correctly both times - the record-tag comment at :283 and the --disc comment at :364 - and then walks into it on the one control a pointer actually presses. The assertion that closed no-pressed-state-anywhere (interaction-check.mjs:1313-1324) reads has("a.kpi:active"), which greps the stylesheet for the selector text and never renders it, so it passes on a rule that cannot paint. Verified in the other direction: forcing .rise to animation-fill-mode: backwards makes hover return matrix(1,0,0,1,0,-2) and press return matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0), with the pre-delay hidden state still holding (opacity 0, translateY(10px) at 60ms under motion=play).
findings.consequence: On a phone there is no hover, so a press is the only channel that can confirm a tap landed - and a tap on a status card produces nothing at all: the owner touches "3 haven't moved in a fortnight" and the surface is pixel-identical. On the desk the cards read as inert panels rather than as the one drill-down the screen offers, so the reader never learns that four of the five cards go somewhere.
findings.fix: Change lately.html:485 from `.rise { animation: rise 0.5s var(--ease) both; ... }` to `.rise { animation: rise 0.5s var(--ease) backwards; ... }`. `backwards` still applies the `from` step through the delay, so nothing is visible before its turn, and it releases the element back to its author styles once the run ends, so :hover and :active paint. Do the same for .dot::before at :357 (`pop 0.4s var(--ease) backwards`) so its transform state is reachable too; leave --disc as it is.
findings.assertion: In every motion mode (settled, play, and both under reducedMotion), after the entrance has finished, hovering a KPI card must move its getBoundingClientRect().top by 2px and holding the pointer down must return it to its rest position - measured from the rendered box, never from the presence of a selector in a stylesheet. Replace the stylesheet grep at interaction-check.mjs:1313-1324 with this rendered measurement for a.kpi, .btn and .dot.

findings.element: --mark-ctx at lately.html:41 (light) and :100 (dark), as painted by .bar at :239 and .dot::before at :357
findings.problem: Composited and measured at 1440 in both grounds: the eleven history columns and the six inside-a-fortnight age dots resolve to #d4d4d8 on #ffffff - 1.48:1 - in light, and #3f3f46 on #18181b - 1.70:1 - in dark. WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of graphical objects required to understand the content, and these are not decoration around the content, they are the content: the twelve-week shape and the nine-mark age distribution. The essential-presentation exception does not reach them, because the lock contains darker zincs that would carry the same reading. Both gates are blind here by construction: audit.mjs's contrast pass reads size, weight and text and only ever judges type (scripts/audit.mjs:244 and :363), and the behaviour gate has no non-text rule at all. For scale, the same measurement puts the live indigo column at 6.29:1 light and 5.94:1 dark, so the surface is carrying a fourfold contrast gap between the mark it wants read and the eleven marks it needs read.
findings.consequence: The dark twin is the clearest case: the ages card states nine open jobs and, to anyone with reduced contrast sensitivity, shows three - the three indigo ones past the fortnight - because the other six sit at 1.70:1 on the ground. The reader is then answering "am I on top of this" from a third of the evidence, with no way of knowing marks are missing. In light the twelve-week chart degrades the same way: one indigo column and eleven that fade out in daylight or on a dimmed laptop.
findings.fix: Add one token from the locked eighteen and point only the marks at it. In :root add `--mark-quiet: #71717a;` and in [data-v="dark"] add `--mark-quiet: #71717a;` (Ink 3 clears the floor against both grounds: 4.83:1 on #ffffff, 3.68:1 on #18181b). Change `.bar { background: var(--mark-ctx) }` at :241 to var(--mark-quiet) and `.dot { --disc: var(--mark-ctx) }` at :349 to var(--mark-quiet). Leave --mark-ctx untouched everywhere else - it also colours .kpi.lead .t-small on the ink plate and .tip s on the ink tooltip, and repointing it globally would drop that 13px caption to 3.91:1. Emphasis survives on three channels the context marks do not have: the live column is darker (6.29:1), it is indigo, and it is hatched.
findings.assertion: Sample the composited fill of every .bar, every .dot::before and every .meter i against its composited backdrop, in both grounds and at 390/768/1280/1440, and require every one of them to reach 3:1. Wire it into audit.mjs as a non-text pass so it runs on every viewport the config declares.

findings.element: the coverage strip's last stamp, shell() at lately.html:904 - Bound workspace, owner, reading date and the ${D.open}
findings.problem: D.open is F.bound.openCount, read unconditionally in the accessor and printed in every state. Driven at 1440 and read back: in `empty` the same strip says "TASKS ANSWERED, NOTHING RECORDED" and then "BOUND WORKSPACE, OWNER, READING DATE AND THE 9". In `error` it says "TASKS DID NOT ANSWER" and then the same 9. In `loading` it says all three sources are "READING" and still prints the 9. The open count is a Tasks-derived figure, so in two of those three the surface prints a number from a source it has just named as silent, one line away, in the same footer. This is not the closed error-state-invents-a-last-good-reading finding: the reading instant is a defensible stamp of when the attempt was made and I am not raising it. The open count is not - it is a reading, not an attempt.
findings.consequence: The honest-degradation contract is that a reader can never mistake "we don't know" for a number, and this breaks it in the two states built to say we don't know. On `empty` the owner is told no work is recorded and shown a 9 in the same frame. On `error` the surface says "Nothing below is shown, because a part of this screen would be guessing" and then guesses, in the footer, three lines down. And because the denominator card is not on screen in any of those three states, "the 9" is a definite reference to a figure that appears nowhere else - the reader cannot even find out what it counts.
findings.fix: Make the stamp state-aware in shell(). Add `const DENOM_STATES = ["full", "partial", "quiet", "first-run"];` beside SOURCES, and replace line 904 with `Bound workspace, owner${DENOM_STATES.includes(state) ? `, reading date and the ${D.open}` : " and reading date"}`. Nothing else in the footer changes.
findings.assertion: In the empty, error and loading states the coverage strip must contain no digit that is not part of the reading time or the reading date. In full, partial, quiet and first-run the count named in the coverage strip must equal the denominator card's numeral (in quiet, the count in its own sentence). Both grounds, all declared viewports.

findings.element: the single .xaxis tick on the first-run chart, lately.html:952, against the .plot.solo rules at :275-277
findings.problem: .plot.solo pins .cols and .baseline to 57px so the one week stands at the pitch it will hold when eleven more arrive, and .xaxis was left out of that treatment. The lone span still carries `flex: 1 1 0; text-align: center` from :313, so it centres itself over the whole plot width rather than over the mark. Driven, the gap between the tick's centre and its column's centre is 108px at 390, 237px at 768, 303px at 900, and 297px at 1024, 1280, 1440 and 1600. The plot is 92% empty at desk widths and the date floats in the middle of that emptiness. This is the same mechanism the r1 fix corrected on the age axis - marks laid out by flexbox instead of standing on their value - surviving on the week axis because .plot.solo constrained two of the three things that had to be constrained.
findings.consequence: The state built for a first-time owner ships a chart in which the only mark and the only date are separated by a third of the card and read as two unrelated objects. Everything the surface knows about when that work happened is in that one label, and it points at white space.
findings.fix: Add one rule beside the other .plot.solo rules at lately.html:277: `.plot.solo + .xaxis { width: 57px; padding-right: 0; }`. The .xaxis is the adjacent sibling of the .plot in both chart() and the first-run block, and the single flex child then centres over the same 57px slot the column and the baseline already occupy.
findings.assertion: In the first-run state, at 390/768/900/1280/1440, the horizontal centre of the week tick must be within 4px of the horizontal centre of the column it labels.

findings.element: .fortnight span, lately.html:375, in the quiet state
findings.problem: The quiet scope's oldest job is 12 days, so D.axisMax rounds to 15 and the fortnight rule lands at 93.3% of the strip. The label is anchored `left: var(--gap-tight)` off the rule with white-space: nowrap, no flip and no clamp, so it is thrown off the right end of the axis at every width. Measured, quiet state, the label's right edge against the ages card's right edge: +55px at 390, +53px at 414, +44px at 560, +30px at 768, +13px at 1024, flush at 1280 and above; against the strip itself it is 72px over at 390 and 24px over at every desk width. At 390 the label's right edge sits at x=421 in a 390px window, so 31px of it is outside the viewport entirely and .canvas's overflow:hidden eats it - the page reports zero horizontal overflow while the text is destroyed, so "no sideways scroll" passes over it. On screen it reads "A FORTN". This is quiet-specific and is not the refuted fortnight-marker-lands-beside-a-fifteen-day-tick: that was about which value the tick carries, this is about the label leaving the card.
findings.consequence: The quiet state's whole claim is "nothing is sitting", and the dashed rule is the evidence for it - the line the reader checks the marks against. On a phone that line arrives unnamed, cut off mid-word with no ellipsis, sitting near the right end of the axis where an unlabelled rule reads as the end of the ruler rather than as a fortnight. The owner is left with an annotation that says nothing and an axis that appears to stop early.
findings.fix: Flip the label inside the rule when it would overrun, measured after layout like everything else on this surface. Add `.fortnight[data-flip] span { left: auto; right: var(--gap-tight); }` beside :375, and in relayout() (lately.html:1069) read the strip's clientWidth and the rule's offsetLeft and set or remove `data-flip` on .fortnight according to whether `ruleLeft + 8 + label.offsetWidth > strip.clientWidth`. relayout() already runs on load, on fonts.ready and on resize, so the three moments that can change the answer are covered.
findings.assertion: In every state that draws the fortnight rule, at 360/390/414/560/768/1024/1280/1440 and in both grounds, the fortnight label's bounding box must sit entirely inside the ages card's content box and entirely inside the viewport.

findings.element:
VIEW.loading at lately.html:975 -
${movementOne() + movementTwo()}
findings.problem: The loading state calls the same movementOne() and movementTwo() the arrived states call, so it is the arrived reading with its ink taken out - not a shape, the numbers. Measured at 1440: the twelve skeleton columns stand at 71/42/84/55/97/71/113/84/84/113/71/168px, which is the weekly series to the pixel; the two gridlines paint real 1px rgba(17,17,17,0.055) borders at the data-derived values 6 and 12; the .record-tag paints a wash box at the previous best's 67% height, because .sk-wrap hides .record at :460 and .record-tag has been a different class since the r1 fix split them; nine dots stand at nine real ages; and the strip's ticks still hold the strings today/15d/30d/45d. Driven with F.weeks and every scope's jobs emptied - the actual condition of a client that is still reading - the file throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'v') and renders nothing at all. The three assertions that guard this state (interaction-check.mjs:374-376) compare that DOM against itself, built from the same fixture in the same frame, and cannot fail: the L-06 class, on rules written to close a real finding.
findings.consequence: The loading state as graded cannot be built, because the client that shows it does not hold the numbers it is drawn from. What ships in its place will be hand-sized again - the exact drift the comment above it records as eliminated, and which measured 48px on the hero and 28px on a card the last time it was written by hand - and no assertion in the gate would see it. For the reader today it also means the surface paints the previous best's position and the whole twelve-week shape while telling them nothing has arrived.
findings.fix: Give the two movements a `skeleton` flag and stop reading D through it: when set, chart() emits twelve columns from a fixed height profile with no gridline values and no record pair, strip() emits nine marks on one row at fixed pitch, and the hero emits a fixed-width block instead of D.lastFour. Guard the accessor so `weeks: F.weeks ?? []` and `jobs: SCOPE.jobs ?? []` cannot throw. Add `.sk-wrap .record-tag, .sk-wrap .gridline { visibility: hidden; }` to :460 so the skeleton hides both halves of a pair rather than one.
findings.assertion: With window.LATELY_FIXTURE.weeks and every scope's jobs emptied, ?state=loading must still render (window.__LATELY_READY true), raise no pageerror, and hold its hero height and its KPI card height within 8px of the arrived layout at 390/768/1280/1440. Run the existing skeleton-geometry assertions against that withheld-data render, not against the arrived one.

findings.element: #retry at lately.html:987 and the empty state's "Open Tasks" button at lately.html:966
findings.problem: Neither control is wired. Over the whole file the string `retry` occurs exactly once, as an id - there is no getElementById("retry"), no delegated handler and no listener that could reach it; the only listeners in the file are resize, scroll, a pointerdown for touch dismissal, the per-mark tip handlers and Escape. Driven: clicking #retry and pressing Enter on it leave main's innerHTML byte-identical (596 chars before and after), the URL unchanged, no aria-busy, no focus move and no announcement. Clicking "Open Tasks" changes nothing either. The id on line 987 is a hook written to be wired and never wired - the code and its own intent disagree inside a single attribute.
findings.consequence: The error state's entire job is to give the owner one move, and pressing it produces nothing at all - not a spinner, not a message, not a re-read. The only reading available is that the product is broken twice: once because Tasks did not answer, and again because the button that was meant to help is dead. The empty state's single instruction has the same problem, and it is also a button where it should be a link, so a screen-reader user is told it is a button and given no destination.
findings.fix: Wire #retry: on click set aria-busy="true" and disabled on the button, write "Reading again" into a role=status element that exists in the static body before render, then location.reload(). Change the empty state's control from `` to `Open Tasks` so it carries a link role and a real destination; the route already exists as a typed constant in src/lib/product-urls.ts.
findings.assertion: Pressing the error state's Try again by mouse and by Enter must change at least one of: the document URL, main's innerHTML, or the control's aria-busy - a press that leaves all three identical fails. The empty state's single control must be an element with an implicit link role whose href resolves to the Tasks route.

findings.element: #tip at lately.html:543 - <div class="tip t-small" id="tip" role="presentation"> - and the <s> it is filled with at :1085
findings.problem: role="presentation" removes only the div's own role; its descendants keep theirs and stay in the accessibility tree. Read out of chromium's full AX tree over CDP at 1440 with the oldest mark focused: StaticText "41 days open" and StaticText "Confirm the marquee sides with the hire company" are both present with ignored:false, alongside the button's own accessible name ("Confirm the marquee sides with the hire company, open 41 days") and the strip's screen-reader sentence, which names all nine again. The tip is also position:fixed outside main and outside every landmark - the shape the r1 coverage-strip finding was about - and its second line is an <s>, whose meaning is content that is no longer accurate.
findings.consequence: A screen-reader user browsing the ages card meets each job's title twice while it holds focus, and one of the two copies is marked up as struck-out content, which in a card about work that has been sitting too long is exactly the wrong implication.
findings.fix: Add aria-hidden="true" to #tip at :543 - the tip's whole content is already carried by each mark's aria-label, so nothing is lost. Change the filled markup at :1085 from <s> to <span class="tip-sub"> and re-key the two rules at :382-383 from `.tip s` to `.tip .tip-sub`.
findings.assertion: With an age mark focused, #tip must contribute no non-ignored node to the accessibility tree, and the number of non-ignored nodes whose name contains that mark's title must be exactly two: the button's name and the strip's screen-reader sentence.

findings.problem: Driven at 1440x960 with real Tab presses: tabbing from the last KPI card to the first age mark scrolls .scroll the minimum distance, which lands the mark at top 948.19 / bottom 960.19 in a 960px window. Its 2px focus ring at 3px offset reaches 965.19 and is clipped by the window edge; .strip-scale runs 963.19 to 980.19 and is entirely below the fold; and because all nine marks then satisfy the browser's minimal-scroll test, the whole keyboard path through the strip happens at that edge with no further scroll. The behaviour gate proves each mark is focusable, named and unoccluded, and never asks where on the screen it lands.
findings.consequence: A keyboard reader crosses all nine marks with the ring cut off at the window edge and with today / 15d / 30d / 45d off-screen. The tooltip still says "41 days open" in words, so the fact survives - but the one thing the strip is drawn to show, where a job sits against the ruler and against the fortnight rule, is unreadable for the entire keyboard path.
findings.fix: Add `scroll-margin-bottom: var(--gap-hall); scroll-margin-top: var(--gap-room);` to the .dot rule at lately.html:348, so the browser's minimal scroll leaves the ruler, the axis and the full ring in view.
findings.assertion: After tabbing to each age mark at 1440x960 and 390x844, the ages card's .strip-scale must be fully inside the viewport and the focused mark's box grown by 5px on every side must be fully inside the viewport.
